answer: Superlinear identity bonding resists sybils: each agent locks a refundable bond that scales with the square of identities tied to one funding source. One honest agent pays a flat fee and registers through a public attestation beacon, while a farm of 1,000 sybils pays about 1,000,000 units, not 1,000. Bonds refund on a slow glacier schedule, so churned stolen identities stay detectable across the sparse tundra of new nodes. To break it an attacker needs 1,000 genuinely unlinkable funding sources, which negates cheap mass minting and makes the n-squared cost dominate.
